section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The ScreenModes module has been extended to pay attention to the limitations of the hardware as provided by the device descriptors. This allows hardware devices with different restrictions on the mode parameters to be catered for by the ScreenModes module. Similarly, the bandwidth restrictions now enforced by the ScreenModes module are provided by the video driver. The original VIDCBandwidthLimit is no longer functional in changing the limits.

The ScreenModes module will always respond to mode enumeration commands with the configuration set by the currently used display. Thus changing the current display will cause a new to be issued to cause clients to re-obtain their list of available modes.
The SWI has been extended to read the DPMS details for the currently configured MDF.

subsection.title: System Sprite Pool
subsection.p: The system sprite pool is no longer controlled by the kernel. This area is now under the control of the SpriteUtils module. With this change, a legacy system call has been removed. This should not affect modern software.
The system sprite area should not be used by modern applications, and this change should not affect any recent software.

swi-definition.name: ScreenModes_ReadInfo
swi-definition.description: Read the DPMS state of the current mode definition

exit.register-use: DPMS state for current mode definition

use.p: This SWI is used to read the DPMS state as configured by the currently selected MDF. This is used by the configuration tools.

swi-definition.name: OS_Byte
swi-definition.description: Read the system sprite area details (OS_Byte 163, 242, 65)

use.p: This call no longer returns the size of the system sprite area. Applications should use to obtain this information.
